- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >50% above recent mean), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 15–30% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is high, model is prone to overconfidence; cap forecasts at 1.5x recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, adjust downward by 0.5–1.0σ.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.8) correlate with underestimation in model; increase forecast by 5–15% when sentiment is high and recent prices are stable.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast if sentiment is >0.50.
- Avoid forecasting >3σ above recent 18-day mean unless sentiment is >0.8; otherwise, apply a “sentiment-adjusted floor” to prevent extreme overestimation.
